story_type: swimmer lowered over whitecaps to a moving fishing boat, litter hoist
hook: He collapsed 30 miles out. The swimmer went down over whitecaps.
narration: Thirty miles south of San Diego, a fisherman collapsed with symptoms like a heart attack.
At eleven fifty-six in the morning, the crew of the fifty-six foot Seeker called the Coast Guard.
A Jayhawk from Sector San Diego lowered its rescue swimmer on the cable, out over the whitecaps and down to the moving boat.
A swimmer straps a patient into a rigid litter, so he can be lifted flat and steady even when the deck is rolling.
Then the litter came up, swinging over the wake toward the door.
Last, the cable went back down for the swimmer.
outcome: The Jayhawk crew hoisted the fisherman aboard, then reeled their swimmer back up through the air.
title: Fisherman collapsed 30 miles out
description:
On July 15, 2014, a Coast Guard Sector San Diego Jayhawk crew lowered a rescue swimmer to the 56-foot fishing boat Seeker about 30 miles south of San Diego and hoisted a fisherman who had collapsed with heart attack like symptoms.
